title: Sri Lanka Sustainability Disclosure Standards SLFRS S1 and SLFRS S2, adopted by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka and published in Gazette Extraordinary No. 2393/31 of 18 July 2024
citation: Sri Lanka Accounting and Auditing Standards Act, No. 15 of 1995, publication under Section 4(2); Gazette Extraordinary No. 2393/31, 2024-07-18
evidence: Gazette Extraordinary No. 2393/31 (English), page 1A, paragraph (a): "The first 100 listed entities of the Colombo Stock Exchange, based on respective entities’ market capitalization as of 01st January, 2025 are required to adopt for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 01st January, 2025." Paragraph (b): all Main Board listed entities, periods beginning on or after 01st January, 2026; paragraph (c): all listed entities except the Empower Board, periods beginning on or after 01st January, 2027; paragraphs (f) and (g) end with 01st January, 2029 and 01st January, 2030. Read from the rendered page image because poppler text of pages 1 and 2 is corrupt. Opened on 2026-11-03.
notes: Stored in the OCR pass 2026-11-03 (the sentences below describe the state before it: they are why the poppler text was not used). The Gazette is the Institute's publication of the adopted standards (71 pages, English; its N.B. says the Sinhala and Tamil versions are published separately, and a search of the site's Gazette Extraordinary list for 'SLFRS' shows only an English file for 2393/31). Poppler output is corrupt on pages 1 and 2, which carry the application schedule (glyph ids with no Unicode map: 'The first' prints as '7KH¿UVW', digits as control characters), and every page's running header is in a legacy Sinhala font (e.g. 'I fldgi ( ^I& fcoh'); pages 3 to 71 extract cleanly. No OCR or font tool is installed in the cloud session, and a record with corrupt or hand-corrected text is not stored, so this instrument is link only. Paragraphs (d) to (g) of the schedule (Empower Board entities, large non-listed companies from 2028 and 2029, other specified business enterprises from 2030) are not transcribed here beyond the dates because the turnover thresholds are among the corrupt characters. The earlier register row cited https://documents.gov.lk/view/egz/2024/7/2393-31_E.pdf, which now answers 404 (the site was rebuilt); the working request is in SOURCES.md. The CSE Listing Rules provision that sets issuer scope was not opened. OCR pass 2026-11-03: one English record, the whole Gazette (pages 1 to 71 of the PDF, every page carries the notice or the standards), is uncorrected OCR output of the page images (extraction ocr; 200 dpi, tesseract 5.3.4 from the Ubuntu package tesseract-ocr 5.3.4-1build5, language pack eng 5.3.4 installed with the package, one run per page, pages joined in order, no text corrected); the PDF text layer was ignored, the running header in the legacy Sinhala font comes out as Latin-letter noise, and misread characters (for example SLFRS S82 for SLFRS S2 in the notice) are in the stored text. No Sinhala or Tamil edition is served by documents.gov.lk for this Gazette (the Gazette says they are published separately), so only English is stored. The standards were adopted by the Institute from the ISSB; the licence row rests on s. 8(b) of the Intellectual Property Act, No. 36 of 2003, which Varun may want to read against the ISSB copyright.

title: National Environmental Act, No. 47 of 1980
citation: National Environmental Act, No. 47 of 1980 (certified 29 October 1980)
evidence: Page 1 of the English PDF (read from the page image): "[Certified on 29th October, 1980]" and section 1: "This Act may be cited as the National Environmental Act, No. 47 of 1980 and shall come into operation on such date as the Minister may appoint by Order published in the Gazette." The appointing Order was not found on the site, so no official page read states the date it came into operation. Opened on 2026-11-03.
notes: Link only. The site serves the Act as passed, in English only (no Sinhala or Tamil file is listed), as a 19-page scan: pdftotext returns no text and no OCR is installed in the cloud session. The site has no consolidation, and the Act as amended (by Act No. 56 of 1988, not on the site, Act No. 53 of 2000 and Act No. 15 of 2026) is not available there. Companion entries: lk-national-environmental-amendment-2000 and lk-national-environmental-amendment-2026. The Act sets up the Central Environmental Authority and licensing of prescribed activities; it contains no climate-change provision that was read. This is the F2 fallback: no Climate Change Act or Bill was found (see lk-national-environmental-amendment-2026 notes). OCR pass 2026-11-03: the 19-page English scan was read with tesseract 5.3.4 at 200 dpi and the output is readable, but no record is stored because the scope entry has no in-force date (the Act came into operation by Ministerial Order that is not on the site) and a record needs one for its file name and commit date; Varun to decide whether the certification date 1980-10-29 may stand in, as it does for Acts with no commencement clause. The site serves English only for this Act.

title: Finance Act, No. 35 of 2018 (Part XI: Carbon Tax)
citation: Finance Act, No. 35 of 2018 (certified 1 November 2018), Part XI, sections 40 to 42 and Third Schedule
evidence: Section 40(1) (Part XI, Carbon Tax): "There shall be levied for every year commencing from January 1, 2019, from the registered owner of every motor vehicle specified in the Third Schedule hereto, a tax to be called the “Carbon Tax”". Cover: "[Certified on 01st of November, 2018]". Opened on 2026-11-03.
notes: Stored: one English translation record, dated 2019-01-01 (the first levy year), holding the whole Act (24 pages, clean text) because the site serves the Act as passed and the stored text is not cut; Part XI is a small part of it. The carbon tax is a levy on motor vehicles collected at annual registration, not an emissions trading system. Section 40(1) was substituted by Finance Act No. 21 of 2019 (lk-finance-act-2019), which limits the levy to 1 January to 30 November 2019. Implementing regulations: lk-finance-carbon-tax-regulations-2019. Languages: the site serves Sinhala, Tamil and English PDFs of this Act. Sinhala and Tamil are stored too (OCR pass 2026-11-03, see the last sentence); the English text is a translation under row LK-GOVPRINT-TRANSLATION. The Act's own clause says the Sinhala text prevails over the Tamil text, so the stored English record is not the prevailing text. The brief named Finance Act No. 11 of 2019 and a 2020 repeal; the official pages read name Finance Act No. 35 of 2018 (Part XI) and No. 21 of 2019, and no repeal Act was found (see lk-finance-act-2019 notes). OCR pass 2026-11-03: the Sinhala record (pages 1 to 25 of the PDF) and the Tamil record (pages 1 to 29) are uncorrected OCR output of the scanned official PDFs (extraction ocr; page images at 200 dpi, tesseract 5.3.4 from the Ubuntu package tesseract-ocr 5.3.4-1build5, language packs tesseract-ocr-sin and tesseract-ocr-tam 4.1.0-2, one run per page, pages joined in order, no text corrected), so misread characters are in the stored text. The PDFs are whole Acts and the records are not cut.

title: Finance Act, No. 21 of 2019 (Part II amends Part XI, Carbon Tax, of Act No. 35 of 2018)
citation: Finance Act, No. 21 of 2019 (certified 31 October 2019), Part II (sections 3 and 4)
evidence: Cover: "[Certified on 31st of October, 2019]". Section 3 substitutes section 40(1) of Act No. 35 of 2018: "There shall be levied a tax to be called the “Carbon Tax” ... for the period commencing from January 1, 2019 and ending on November 30, 2019, from the registered owner of every motor vehicle specified in the Third Schedule". Only Part IV (section 6) has its own commencement clause, so Part II takes the certification date. Opened on 2026-11-03.
notes: Stored: one English translation record, whole Act (clean text). Its Part II ends the Carbon Tax levy period on 2019-11-30; the other Parts amend Parts VII and XII of Act No. 35 of 2018 and add a levy on foreign commercial transactions. No Act restoring the tax was found: the 238 English Acts dated 2019 to 2026 that the site lists were fetched on 2026-11-03 and 178 of them have a text layer; searched for 'carbon', 'climate change' and 'greenhouse', the only Acts that use these words for anything but chemistry or hydrocarbons are this Act, the Sri Lanka Electricity Act No. 36 of 2024 (decarbonisation goals) and the Tea Research Board (Amendment) Act No. 8 of 2019; the other 60 Acts are scans and were not searched. A formal repeal of Part XI (the brief mentions 2020) was not found: the Finance (Amendment) Act No. 2 of 2020 amends section 36 only. The tax therefore lapsed by its own limited period (1 January to 30 November 2019) on the official pages read. Languages: the site serves Sinhala, Tamil and English PDFs of this Act. Sinhala and Tamil are stored too (OCR pass 2026-11-03, see the last sentence); the English text is a translation under row LK-GOVPRINT-TRANSLATION. The Act's own clause says the Sinhala text prevails over the Tamil text, so the stored English record is not the prevailing text. OCR pass 2026-11-03: the Sinhala record (pages 1 to 11 of the PDF) and the Tamil record (pages 1 to 14) are uncorrected OCR output of the scanned official PDFs (extraction ocr; page images at 200 dpi, tesseract 5.3.4 from the Ubuntu package tesseract-ocr 5.3.4-1build5, language packs tesseract-ocr-sin and tesseract-ocr-tam 4.1.0-2, one run per page, pages joined in order, no text corrected), so misread characters are in the stored text. The PDFs are whole Acts and the records are not cut.

title: Finance (Carbon Tax) Regulations, No. 1 of 2019 (Gazette Extraordinary No. 2105/47, 11 January 2019)
citation: Finance (Carbon Tax) Regulations, No. 1 of 2019, made under sections 41(3) and 51 of the Finance Act, No. 35 of 2018; Gazette Extraordinary No. 2105/47
evidence: Gazette Extraordinary No. 2105/47 of 11 January 2019: "BY virtue of the powers vested in me by Section 41 (3) read with Section 51 of the Finance Act, No. 35 of 2018, I, Mangala Samaraweera, Minister of Finance and Mass Media, do by this Order prescribe the following regulations." signed "11th January, 2019". The regulations have no commencement clause, so the Gazette date is used. Opened on 2026-11-03.
notes: Stored in the OCR pass 2026-11-03 (the sentences below describe the state before it). One-page Gazette; the body extracts cleanly with pdftotext but its first line is the running header in a legacy Sinhala font ('I fldgi ( ^I& fPoh - YS% ,xld ...'), which is corrupt, and a record with a corrupt line or a hand-removed line is not stored. The regulations say the tax is paid by the registered owner and collected by the Divisional Secretary or the Provincial Commissioner of Motor Traffic and remitted to the Consolidated Fund; they set no rate. title: Consumer Affairs Authority Act, No. 9 of 2003 (sections 30 and 31: misleading or deceptive conduct, false representations)
citation: Consumer Affairs Authority Act, No. 9 of 2003 (certified 17 March 2003), ss. 30 and 31
evidence: Cover: "[Certified on 17th March, 2003]"; section 1 gives the short title only and the Act has no commencement clause, so the certification date is used. Section 30: "No trader shall, in the course of a trade or business, engage in any type of conduct that is misleading or deceptive or is likely to mislead or deceive the consumer or any other trader." Section 31 makes a trader guilty of an offence who falsely represents goods or services in the ways listed in paragraphs (a) to (g). Opened on 2026-11-03.
notes: Stored: one English translation record, the whole Act (53 pages, clean text). The Act has no environmental-claims provision; ss. 30 and 31 are the general umbrella, and the Act is listed as the F6 fallback for that reason. Amended by Act No. 20 of 2021 (lk-caa-amendment-2021). Languages: the site lists a Sinhala PDF (59 pages, a scan with no text layer, stored in the OCR pass 2026-11-03) and the English PDF; no Tamil file is listed. The Act says the Sinhala text prevails over the Tamil text (section 76), so the stored English record is not the prevailing text. OCR pass 2026-11-03: the Sinhala record (pages 1 to 59 of the PDF, the whole Act) is uncorrected OCR output of the scanned official PDF (extraction ocr; 200 dpi, tesseract 5.3.4 from the Ubuntu package tesseract-ocr 5.3.4-1build5, language pack tesseract-ocr-sin 4.1.0-2, one run per page, pages joined in order, no text corrected), so misread characters are in the stored text. The Sinhala text is the prevailing one under section 76.
